set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 quality review, verified by exhaustive grep across main and test.

Problem:
ResultContractDescriptor (core/Workload.scala:95-100) declares maxBytes: ByteLimit. There is no read of resultContract.maxBytes, descriptor.maxBytes or contract.maxBytes anywhere in modules/ or tools/, in main or in test. Result payloads are actually bounded by a separate maximumResultBytes carried on the remote options (ssh/RemoteBatch.scala:24, RemoteTask.scala:73).

So the field is inert, and it is inert in the way that matters: it is publicly settable through ResultContractDescriptor.from, which validates schema and declaredOutputs against the mode but places no constraint on maxBytes. A caller can set it, reasonably believe they have bounded their result, and get no bound.

Consequences already visible:
- AgentDomainJson.encodeSubmitRequest (:35-56) does not put it on the wire, and decodeSubmitRequest (:78) substitutes ResultContract.ExitOnly.descriptor, so the value does not survive a round trip.
- Because it is absent from the canonical bytes, two LaunchSpecs differing only in maxBytes produce the same CanonicalRequest digest and are treated by the managed controller as the same request rather than a conflict.

Neither of those is a live bug today, precisely because nothing reads the field. That is the point: the codec gap is a symptom, and putting the field on the wire would preserve a value that still has no effect.

Decision required, not a fix:
(a) delete the field and let maximumResultBytes be the single bound, or
(b) give it meaning at the point results are read and then put it on the wire and in the digest.

Either resolves the codec asymmetry as a side effect. Do not close this by only adding the wire field.

Acceptance: the descriptor has no field that a caller can set without effect, and whichever bound survives is the one enforced when a result is read.
set.title: P8.D8: Resolve ResultContractDescriptor.maxBytes, a public field nothing reads
